questions.prompt: Using the nearest-rank method, what is the p90 of these 20 response times?
questions.explanation: Rank = ceil(0.90 × 20) = 18. The 18th smallest value in the sorted list is 190.

questions.prompt: Why does p99 matter even if only 1% of requests are that slow?
options: A user who makes many requests per session is very likely to hit at least one slow one
p99 is always equal to the mean
It is required by HTTP
It measures throughput
questions.explanation: If a page makes 50 requests, the chance that all are under p99 is 0.99^50 ≈ 60%, so about 40% of page loads include a p99-slow call.

questions.prompt: Which statements about combining percentiles are true? Select all that apply.
options: You cannot average p95s from different servers to get the combined p95
Merging raw samples or histograms gives a correct combined percentile
The overall p95 is always the max of the servers' p95s
Percentiles from different time windows cannot simply be averaged either
questions.explanation: Percentiles are not additive. Correct combination needs raw data or mergeable histograms. The combined p95 lies between the servers' values but is not generally the max.

questions.prompt: A closed-model load tool waits for each response before sending the next request. The server freezes for 5 s once. Why might the tool's p99 understate what real users experienced?
options: Coordinated omission: during the freeze the tool stopped sending, so the many requests real users would have sent were never measured
The tool rounds numbers
p99 is too strict
The freeze was in the network
questions.explanation: Real users keep arriving during a stall. A closed tool records one slow sample instead of hundreds, so the tail looks far better than reality. Open-model arrival rates or correction techniques help.

questions.prompt: The SLO is "p95 < 500 ms over each 5-minute window". The overall 1-hour p95 is 420 ms. Can you declare the SLO met?
options: No; check each 5-minute window, because a bad window can be hidden in the hourly percentile
Only if the mean is also below 500
Only for GET requests
questions.explanation: The SLO is defined per window. A 10-minute incident can breach it while barely moving the hourly p95.
